# Native colour-ID fixture

`regions.fbx` contains two triangles with explicit indexed polygon-corner
colours, face materials and separate UV0 islands: black and white. It is generated test data,
not an octopus asset or downstream material acceptance.

`ColorID.png` was generated by installed official Substance 3D 16.0.0
(build 10849) through typed DCC-MCP `bake_color_map`, using CPU, UV0, the same
mesh as high and low geometry, padding 4 and mip diffusion disabled. Both
vertex-colour and material-colour modes produced the same native image. Native
output is 256 x 256, RGBA, 16-bit. Both native renders were byte-identical and
had zero native warnings.

Complete native 16-bit readback measured black and white at both triangle
centroids and resolved interior texels, with alpha 1 and error 0. This limited
fixture verifies explicit colour-ID baking, not arbitrary mesh/UV coverage.

SHA256:

- `regions.fbx`: `ac83ce4813075c36942aed9613ba40b073e809c0150cef757c1fd6fd2576243b`
- `ColorID.png`: `df8739b04319fa72dfc2e51df9bc911a2994fd3bc276090f9f8ef12bf09b311a`
- `substance3d_baker.exe`: `aab9eb495b641e59b48400329320d72987cf9a17af1180c5e2e8960fa20f28d2`

The native PNG is retained unchanged; Python did not create or postprocess it.
